thread:
anna: Noticed a weird class of fncall rejects in staging this morning. Validator complains 'unexpected_type: array' for the orders.create tool. Root call shows the fallback variant was used. Anyone seen arrays from orders-adapter before?

pete: yep. legacy behavior: when no order items returned, adapter used to return `[]` instead of `{items: []}`. We thought the adapter rewrite fixed it, but looks like the fallback model is emitting an empty array in a few traces.

li: can we add an explanatory breadcrumb in the trace UI that surfaces "was_fallback=true" and the fallback_variant id? Right now trace only shows the route id which isn't enough.

sam: also we need better telemetry for billing: are rejects that happen pre-tool-invoke being labeled as tool usage? billing team flagged a potential mismatch yesterday.

billing-bot: billing: FYI customers will be invoiced for tool time only if `telemetry.events.invoked_tool=true`. Current schema: invoked_tool may be null for rejects. Please standardize.

anna: action: make `invoked_tool` mandatory for fncall events (true/false). If false, set `tool_tokens=0` in billing ingestion.

pete: short mitigation: gateway can coerce `[]` -> `{items: []}` for orders.create responses only, add `coerced=true` flag. That buys time while we patch fallback/model.

li: please add a dashboard card: "fncall.rejects by reason" with a tag for `coerced=true|false` and `was_fallback=true|false`. I want to see if coercion hides a larger problem.

deploy-bot: sample-capture started cap_1820. redaction enabled.

sam: telemetry ask: include `validator_name`, `validator_version`, `route_id`, `fallback_variant`, `invoked_tool`, and `coerced` in the fncall.reject event. Also attach `sample_id` when available.

pete: will add fields to the event schema and backfill for the last 12h.

anna: UX: add a small "contract diff" view in the rollout console that shows example adapter response vs expected schema (highlight missing keys / extra arrays). Even a one-line summary would help during canaries.

li: propose we wire an automated preflight check in rollout: run 200 synthetic requests and assert 99.9% contract pass vs adapter stubs. If check fails, block promotion.

sam: +1. Also create an alert: if `coerced=true` > 0.2% for 30m in any region then page the oncall for platform. We don't want coercion to be our permanent bandaid.

billing-bot: billing-ops: will add a dashboard row to show potential misattribution where `invoked_tool=null`.

anna: ok plan recap in order: 1) deploy coercion middleware for orders.create (canary 5%), add `coerced` tag; 2) enforce mandatory `invoked_tool` boolean on fncall events + billing backfill; 3) add dashboard card and alert for coerced vs rejects; 4) rollout console: contract-diff quick view + preflight synthetic test.

pete: starting PR for coercion middleware. will include `coerced_by='gateway'` label.

li: I'll own dashboard and console bits. Sam, can you own alerts and synthetic runner?

sam: yes. I'll also add the sample ingestion pipeline to compute a short `shape_signature` (e.g., `object:items[]` vs `array`) and persist as a tag.

deploy-bot: canary rollout of coercion middleware v0.2 -> slice=5% started. monitor: fncall.rejects, fncall.coercion.count, billing.invoked_tool_rate.

anna: thanks. keep this thread updated with sample ids and dashboard links. If we see `coerced` > 0.2% after 1h we escalate to a rollback. :thumbsup:
